question: One type of brake has a diaphragm operating in a cylinder. For one side, one diaphragm uses atmospheric pressure and the other side, the brake where negative pressure is applied by exhaust air, is called ____ brake.
solution:
The correct answer is __Vacuum**(Vacuum)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vacuum brake__ is a braking system commonly used in railways and some vehicles.
 
• It operates using atmospheric pressure on one side and a vacuum (negative pressure) on the other.
 
• The diaphragm creates the force required for braking by utilizing the pressure differential.
 
• Vacuum brakes are reliable and suitable for long trains due to their simplicity.
 
• They require maintenance to ensure proper vacuum levels and prevent air leaks.
 
• Modern trains have largely replaced vacuum brakes with air brakes for enhanced efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Air Brake:**
 
 
• Uses compressed air to create braking force.
 
• Widely used in modern trains and heavy vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Hydraulic Brake:**
 
 
• Uses hydraulic fluid to transfer force from the brake pedal to the braking mechanism.
 
• Commonly used in automobiles for effective braking.
 
 
 
• **Electric Brake:**
 
 
• Uses electrical energy to provide braking, often combined with regenerative systems.
 
• Found in electric vehicles and some advanced railway systems.
